title: Intersectional Bias in Japanese Large Language Models from a Contextualized Perspective

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model responses to multiple-choice question-answering prompts in the inter-JBBQ dataset, featuring profiles that combine multiple intersecting social attributes in ambiguous and disambiguated contexts.
Comparing model predictions on ambiguous multiple-choice questions involving profiles with varying gender identities (e.g., male, female, transgender) while controlling for other social attributes.
Assessing model choices in QA tasks using templates where profile subjects have different nationalities or countries of origin combined with other attributes.
Testing model outputs on QA prompts featuring subjects of different racial backgrounds combined with other demographic attributes.
Evaluating model responses to profiles varying by employment status, occupation, and salary levels in context-specific scenarios like housing issues and marriage markets.
Measuring stereotype associations by testing QA prompts with profiles that differ by educational background (e.g., middle school education vs. university degree).
Assessing model bias using multiple-choice QA templates that include profiles varying by age groups (e.g., 20s vs. 60s) alongside other intersecting attributes.
Evaluating model choices on QA prompts containing profiles with varying sexual orientations (e.g., lesbian, pansexual) combined with other attributes.
